svg.text: Handling Imbalance: Token Dropping vs MegaBlocks Dropless MoE
Fixed expert capacity forces token dropping or memory padding. MegaBlocks uses block-sparse GPU kernels.
Standard MoE: Fixed Capacity & Dropping
Capacity C = CF × (k · B · s) / E
Rigid tensor shapes require uniform buffer size C
• Overloaded experts exceed capacity C:
→ Excess tokens are dropped (bypass MLP via residual).
→ Dropped tokens degrade language modeling accuracy.
• Underloaded experts receive fewer than C tokens:
→ Buffers must be padded with zeros (wasting memory & FLOPs).
→ High capacity factors (CF = 1.5–2.0) inflate GPU memory.
MegaBlocks: Dropless Block-Sparse MoE
Block-Sparse Matrix Kernels (dMoE)
Dynamic ragged tensor execution (Gale et al., MLSys 2023)
• Zero token dropping: 100% of tokens processed.
→ Preserves downstream reasoning and factual recall.
• Zero padding waste: Variable-sized blocks allocated.
→ Experts compute only on tokens actually received.
• Throughput: Achieves up to 40% faster end-to-end
training than padded baselines (Tutel, Megatron-LM).
Production Standard: Modern open-weights MoE models (Mixtral 8x7B, DeepSeek-V2/V3) universally use dropless MoE,
eliminating token dropping entirely to avoid sacrificing model quality during pretraining.
